 HONOLULU (Island News) -- Former Honolulu prosecutor Katherine Kealoha is scheduled to be released to a halfway house this month after she was convicted in 2019 in a mailbox framing scheme, according to confirmation from the Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP).
 Katherine Kealoha was sentenced in 2020 to 13 years in federal prison for her role in a public corruption conspiracy involving her husband, former Honolulu Police Chief Louis Kealoha, and former police officers. Retired federal public defender Alexander Silvert confirmed via BOP on Wednesday her halfway house release on Nov. 20, 2026 following the high-profile public corruption case.
 A federal jury convicted the Kealohas and two former officers in 2019 of conspiracy and attempted obstruction of justice for framing Katherine Kealoha’s uncle, Gerard Puana, for stealing the couple’s mailbox.
 Prosecutors said the scheme was intended to discredit and intimidate Puana after he accused Katherine Kealoha of stealing money from him and his elderly mother. Evidence at trial showed the couple took more than $148,000 from the grandmother’s accounts over six months.
 Katherine was sentenced to 156 months in prison, while Louis received an 84-month sentence.
 The case was one of Hawaii’s largest public corruption investigations and raised questions about abuses of power within the Honolulu Police Department and the state’s justice system.
